Definition: Explicit classification of export behavior into exported, omitted, approximated, delegated, unsupported, or tbd categories per DEL-17-02.
Notes: Shared DEL-17-02 taxonomy across export builders

Definition: A metadata object asserting human review is required and that the software makes no release, compatibility, validation, compliance, certification, sealing, or approval claim.

Synonyms: sidecar mapping; stable_id_map; sidecar id map
Definition: An authoritative side artifact correlating canonical IDs to target records without asserting direct ID carriage in the target format.
Deliverable and document references establishing the provenance authority basis for an export package or profile.
Authority or lifecycle wording (e.g. approval, certification, sealed, validated, compliant) screened out of user-controlled handoff metadata.
Deterministic JSON serialization with sorted keys and ASCII output used as the byte basis for checksums.
A normalized record fixing unit, coordinate, stable-ID, and loss-report policies plus source-basis and carried TBD references for an export package.
Deterministic ASCII piping component file text rendered for a conservative invented straight-pipe subset, terminated by an END-ISOGEN record.
A stable minimal MBF-style ASCII text payload (UNITS, NODES, ELEMENTS, SUPPORTS, LOAD_CASES, END) rendered from invented CAEPIPE smoke-subset records.
The lifecycle state of an adapter export target: candidate_non_gating, source_basis_pending, source_basis_admitted, rejected, quarantined, or tbd.
A requested runtime capability (filesystem, network, process, etc.) recorded as denied by default in the export adapter SDK foundation.
A non-authoritative DEL-15-04 metadata envelope recording references, attachments, assumptions, and unsupported flags without invoking external tools.
A project-owned DEL-17-03 interchange artifact preserving model identity, stable IDs, units, provenance, and loss reporting.
A record of model, result, and target export units plus conversion policy, performed flag, and scope for an export package.
